text:
julia: ran a few nsys + perfetto captures on the regression PR, attaching the top-level observations here

sam: thanks — quick summary?

julia: big takeaway: the nvtx timeline is *full* of tiny push/pop ranges around every kernel launch (thousands per request). overhead looks non-trivial when we do small batches. also KV cache prefetch ranges are interleaved which makes the kernel selection story noisy.

emma: are those NVTX ranges generated by the runtime tracer or by the kernel launcher?

julia: runtime tracer, we push a small range around each kernel selection and then another around the kernel call. code sketch: ```nvtxRangePushA("k:conv_fwd"); launch_kernel(...); nvtxRangePopA();```

david: that's what I feared. NVTX push/pop per tiny kernel will add latency at scale. options: 1) collapse to per-request anchors + emit sampled kernel markers (perfetto slices or NVTX markers not ranges), 2) coalesce contiguous kernel spans into a single range, 3) emit short markers with metadata rather than full ranges.

sam: agree. for perf analysis we still need kernel-level visibility for hotspot attribution, but we don't need NVTX to carry the full per-kernel duration in realtime. suggestion: keep a top-level request span `req:<id>` for tracing and then annotate a separate perfetto track with kernel events (instant events) so timelines stay readable.

julia: prototype idea: create two primitives in tracer: 
- push_request_span(req_id) -> long NVTX range (low frequency)
- record_kernel_event(kernel_name, attrs) -> perfetto instant / NVTX marker (no push/pop)

emma: that would let perfetto/nvprof/nsys still attribute kernels to the request via the request_id tag without millions of short NVTX ranges. we can also tag kernel events with `kernel_selector_hint` and `batch_size` so mapping to kernel-selection decisions is easier.

david: on batching heuristics: we should also log batch-coalescing boundaries as events (e.g., `batch_group: [2,3,5]`) so when we inspect the timeline we can correlate spikes with specific batch groups.

perf-bot: nsys command used by julia: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt -o /tmp/run.nsys ./run_perf_test --cfg small-batches`

sam: concrete NVTX naming convention proposal (short, machine-friendly):
- request span: `req:<short-id>`
- request phase: `req:<id>/phase:<prepare|enqueue|serve|kv_prefetch|finish>`
- kernel instant: `k|<arch>|<op>|b=<batch>` (e.g., `k|ampere|conv_fwd|b=3`)
- kernel ranges (coalesced): `k-range|<reason>|<agg-count>`

julia: love short names. we should also standardize a small set of keys we parse out (id, batch, selector) so the trace consumer code can link to the kernel selection logs. no free-form strings.

emma: about KV cache: the prefetch code currently emits one NVTX range per page fetched. can we instead emit a single `kv:prefetch` range per request and record per-page events? that's same pattern and reduces nvtx overhead.

david: yes. and for kernel selection, produce a JSON blob per request in the trace metadata track showing the selected kernel sequence and thresholds used (fallbacks, quantization flags). that avoids needing to encode heavy info into the NVTX strings.

sam: instrumentation performance test plan:
1) baseline (current nvtx per-kernel) 
2) request-span + kernel-instants + coalesced-kv 
3) request-span + sampled-kernel-ranges (emit ranges only for 1/100 requests)
measure p50/p95 latency and nsys overhead (trace capture disabled vs enabled).

julia: I'll run the above and push a small prototype tracer update (no behavioral changes) to a feature branch. will capture both nsys and perfetto links.

perf-bot: note: nsys captures with many NVTX ranges can blow up the file size quickly, prefer perfetto proto for long runs and nsys for short repros.

emma: one more quick thought: if we want to preserve perfetto flamegraph friendliness, make kernel instant names consistent and short so downstream tools can collapse them. e.g., `k:sgemm_b3` instead of long descriptive name.

david: agreed. also ensure each event includes a `span_id` numeric tag (64-bit hex) — trivial to add to nvtxRangePushAttributes or perfetto metadata. that will let us do precise joins without parsing names.

sam: ok. next steps: julia will post the prototype branch + nsys/perfetto captures; we'll run the three test configs and reconvene to decide which pattern to adopt.

julia: thanks all, will post updates in this thread when captures are uploaded. :white_check_mark:
